profile.entities: Greenlam Industries Limited (consolidated). Two-brand consolidation completed in FY26: **Mikasa** (plywood, laminates, veneers, flooring, doors) and **Greenlam** (flagship laminates + melamine chipboard) — earlier brands Greenlam/NewMika/Mikasa/Decowood folded into these two. 5 factories (laminates: Andhra Pradesh + Gujarat; plus plywood and chipboard plants).
profile.mgmt: Saurabh Mittal (MD & CEO — primary voice); Ashok Sharma (CFO — financials)
profile.subseg: Laminate & Allied (high-pressure laminates, compact laminates — flagship); Plywood & Allied (plywood, decorative veneer, engineered floors, engineered doors); Panel & Allied (melamine chipboard / particle board incl. pre-laminated, HMR)

deepdive.sec: Building Materials / Interior Surfaces & Wood-Panel (laminates, plywood, decorative veneer, engineered floors & doors, melamine chipboard/particle board)

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging mode: net debt INR 940 cr → guide ~INR 50 cr reduction in FY27.
- Reinvestment now modest (brownfield only); priority is converting prior capex into revenue/profit (operating leverage) rather than fresh expansion.
- Brand consolidation to two brands (Greenlam, Mikasa) to reduce brand/channel cost.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **New-business breakeven slippage:** plywood (FY26 EBITDA loss INR 29.5 cr) and chipboard (INR 23 cr) must hit FY27 breakeven for the PAT story to work — chipboard hinges on utilization climbing past ~50%.
- **Demand softness:** weak secondary sales, tight dealer cash flows, project postponement after April price hikes; building-material-wide cost inflation (steel, cement, paint, laminate, ply) could dent volumes.
- **RM/chemical volatility** tied to the West Asia conflict; export logistics (longer transit, higher sea freight both ways); Middle East demand hit in March-April (May normalized).
- **Plywood realization capped** (already near category top; no Tier-2/mid-price entry planned) — growth must come from volume/pan-India, which is deferred to FY28.
- **Competitive intensity:** consolidation favors large players (Greenlam benefits), but unorganized/mid-size disruption and possible particle-board→MDF capacity shifts (mgmt unaware of any) are sector watch-items.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Candid and operationally detailed. MD openly framed FY26 as a "first full year of execution" after three build-out years, and was transparent that PAT weakness is new-business drag, not core erosion. CFO declined to disclose pre-lam share (to be shared offline) — minor opacity. Confident, low-promotional tone; treats the geopolitical crisis as a market-share opportunity ("whenever there's a crisis, we've won share"). Guidance is specific and falsifiable (18-20% top line, FY27 ply+chipboard breakeven, end-FY27 line commissioning) — good for next-quarter accountability.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The "-18% PAT" headline masks a record core: laminates did ~INR 400 cr EBITDA and ~16% margin; the entire profit decline is start-up losses + first-year interest/depreciation on assets that are now in place — a classic operating-leverage inflection if FY27 breakevens land.
- Greenlam's chipboard bet is really a **QCO/formalization + off-site-carpentry** structural call: branded melamine particle board taking share as Indian furniture manufacturing industrializes, mirroring Europe.
- Laminate growth is deliberately a **market-share grind** ("inch-by-inch"), especially in Europe where the industry isn't growing organically — Greenlam's edge is distribution + warehouses + on-ground teams, not end-market tailwind.
- Pricing power asymmetry: full domestic RM pass-through vs only ~4-5% in exports (offset by rupee) — a weaker rupee is a quiet margin cushion on exports.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt at INR 995 crores as of Sept 2025; net debt-to-equity at 0.88x as of FY25, reflecting elevated leverage post capex.
- Maiden bonus equity shares issued in FY25 (1:1 ratio), signaling confidence in long-term shareholder value creation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Laminate & Allied (core, ~80% of revenue):** Q4 revenue INR 658 cr (+14% YoY); FY26 INR 2,433 cr (+9.3%). Q4 EBITDA margin (pre-forex) 17.2% (+350 bps YoY); FY 15.9% (+210 bps). FY26 laminate EBITDA ~INR 400 cr (one of the highest ever). Q4 production 4.87m sheets at 79% utilization; sales 5.15m sheets (+4.5%); avg realization INR 1,243/sheet. FY: production 21.01m sheets at 86% utilization; sales 20.65m sheets (+4.6%); realization INR 1,144/sheet. Peak achievable utilization ~108-110% annual (mix-dependent).
- **Plywood & Allied (plywood, decorative veneer, engineered floors, engineered doors):** Q4 revenue INR 119 cr (+18% YoY), EBITDA loss (pre-forex) INR 3.8 cr; FY26 revenue INR 400 cr (+18.4%), EBITDA loss INR 29.5 cr. Premium-only positioning; ply realization Q4 INR 246/sq m, FY INR 257/sq m (not expected to rise much — already near top of category). ~2.5 years in business; ~45-50% utilization in Q4.
- **Panel & Allied (chipboard / particle board):** Q4 revenue INR 80 cr (+47% QoQ), EBITDA loss (pre-forex) INR 2.2 cr; FY26 revenue INR 213 cr, EBITDA loss INR 23 cr. Q4 production 35,300 cbm at 49% utilization (highest of the year); Q4 sales 38,800 cbm (+34% QoQ) at INR 20,562/cbm; FY production 113,450 cbm at 39% utilization, sales ~110,000 cbm at INR 19,370/cbm. First full year of operation; "amongst the top players" in year one. HMR launched Q3; matching edge-band launched Q4.

latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard (track QoQ/YoY)

latest_quarter.body:
- **RM:** war-driven chemical cost spike from March; largely passed on (full domestic; ~4-5% in exports + rupee-depreciation cushion + contractual freight pass-through). Since then chemical costs softened slightly and minor price corrections were taken — Q4 gross margin fell 410 bps QoQ on the input-cost rise before that softening.
- **Laminate** is the margin engine (~16-17%); plywood & chipboard are currently dilutive but converging to breakeven.
- **Operating leverage** is the thesis: with capex done, rising utilization (laminate 86%→peak ~108-110%; ply toward full by FY28; chipboard 39%→improving) should lift EBITDA and PAT.
- Interest & depreciation elevated (first full year on new plants) — net debt INR 940 cr to be trimmed ~INR 50 cr.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** FY26 crossed INR 3,000 cr revenue (INR 3,046 cr, +18.6%); Q4 record INR 858 cr (+26%). Laminate FY EBITDA ~INR 400 cr (margin ~16%; Q4 ~17.2%). PAT INR 56 cr (-18%) on plywood (-INR 29.5 cr) & chipboard (-INR 23 cr) EBITDA losses + higher interest/depreciation. Net debt INR 940 cr. Brand consolidation to Greenlam + Mikasa completed. Guidance: FY27 ~18-20% top line, laminate ~10-12%, plywood & chipboard EBITDA breakeven in FY27, 2 brownfield AP laminate lines (+2m sheets) by end-FY27, net debt -~INR 50 cr.
- _Next Q → check: (1) chipboard utilization past ~50% / EBITDA breakeven; (2) plywood loss narrowing toward breakeven; (3) AP laminate line commissioning on track for end-FY27; (4) demand — did the April price hikes dent volumes? (5) net-debt reduction tracking; (6) laminate margin holding ~16-17%; (7) Middle East export recovery._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** ~18-20% consol top-line in FY27 (reiterated multi-year ~18% trajectory) despite RM costs and possible demand disruption. **Laminates specifically ~10-12%** growth in FY27.
- **Margin:** Laminate EBITDA (before forex) ~16-17% sustainable, "may go up over time." Plywood and chipboard both targeted to reach **EBITDA breakeven within FY27** (chipboard breakeven ~50% utilization; Q4 chipboard loss already down to ~INR 2 cr).
- **Capacity:** 2 new laminate lines at Andhra Pradesh (+2 million sheets) commissioning **end of FY27** — brownfield; no fifth laminate plant needed; no other new capacity in FY27 (focus = sweat existing assets).
- **Plywood footprint:** stays regional (South, parts of West & East) in FY27; **pan-India only from ~FY28**; near-full utilization of existing ply plant expected by ~FY28.
- **Debt:** reduce net debt ~INR 50 cr in FY27.
- **Chipboard:** pre-lamination share rising toward an ambition of ~100% of production laminated; more premium pre-lam products (HMR launched Q3; matching edge-band launched Q4).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Not an order-book business (B2B/B2C building-materials distribution). Demand visibility is channel-driven: management reports secondary sales "a bit weak," tight dealer cash flows, and some project postponement after the April price hikes — but **no demand destruction** seen by the company itself; "mixed bag."
- Exports: present in ~120 countries; not chasing new geographies in FY27 (deepening existing). Europe positioning strong — 2 warehouses (Italy, Germany) + own teams in Germany, Italy, Spain, Poland, Romania; the 2 new laminate lines are aimed largely at European market.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Chipboard / melamine particle board** is the structural optionality: management argues **QCO (Quality Control Order) implementation** for furniture/furniture products will formalize the market and shift volume toward branded melamine chipboard (Europe-style substrate adoption — wardrobes, kitchens, shop fit-outs, office/residential furniture). Tailwind from **off-site/factory carpentry** displacing on-site carpentry.
- Pre-lamination value-mix uplift (toward ~100% laminated, premium decors/textures/HMR).
- European laminate share-gain (the 2 new AP lines target Europe; organic growth there is flat, so it's a market-share story vs local producers).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Greenlam crossed INR 3,000 cr revenue in FY26 (+18.6%) — its first full year of just running the five plants it spent FY23–25 building — with the core laminates engine printing a record ~INR 400 cr EBITDA (FY26 laminate margin ~16%, Q4 exit ~17%), while the two new businesses (Plywood & Allied, chipboard) are still pre-breakeven and dragged PAT down 18% to INR 56 cr on their losses plus higher interest and depreciation. The investable inflection is operating leverage: management guides FY27 to ~18% top-line growth with no new major capacity (only 2 brownfield laminate lines coming end-FY27) and expects both plywood and chipboard to hit EBITDA breakeven in FY27 — i.e. the loss-making drag turns neutral-to-positive just as the heavy-capex phase ends.

open.item: Working capital cycle maintained at 57 days for FY26 despite new chipboard business, and improved to 51 days in Q4.
Laminate segment contributed about 80% of revenue in H1 FY26; expected to remain core as other businesses scale.
Gross margin improved to 55.5% in Q3FY26, one of the highest levels, driven by pricing discipline and value addition.
Chipboard production utilization was 41% in Q3FY26 and 36% for 9MFY26.
Laminate production utilization was 83% in Q3FY26 and 88% for 9MFY26.
Net debt stood at INR1,010 crores as on 31st December 2025.
Working capital cycle improved by 9 days to 58 days in Q3FY26 vs 67 days in Q3FY25.
Launched high moisture resistant chipboard and a lower-priced plywood variant BWP+ to improve value mix and market reach.
Chipboard utilization reached 49% in Q4FY26, the highest in the year, and is expected to keep improving.
Q4FY26 revenue expected to be decent, similar to Q2FY26 levels, with 18% topline growth.
Full-year FY26 revenue growth expected around 18-20%, possibly 1% lower, despite demand challenges.
Remaining capex of INR50-75 crores to be spent, mostly in Q4FY26 and any leftover in Q1FY27.
FY26 is a year of execution, free from expansions of the last three years, with complete focus on execution across businesses.
Become water positive by 2027 and reduce water intensity by 20%.
Management expects to maintain ~18% top-line growth in FY27 despite raw material cost increases and possible demand disruption.
Laminates segment top-line growth expected in the 10-12% range for FY27.
Two new laminate lines at the Andhra Pradesh plant will come into production by end of FY27.
Plywood and Allied segment expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in FY27.
Net debt expected to be reduced by approximately INR50 crores in FY27.
No new capacity additions in FY27 beyond the two laminate lines; focus on converting existing investments into revenue and profitability.
